rationale: Colour-and-holes pairs distinguish the hole-free colour-2 objects, which become 6 in demonstrations 2 and 3, from colour-1 and colour-3 objects, which retain their colours.
Size rank selects the recolouring: demonstration 1 changes ranks 1 and 3 to 6 and rank 4 to 7; demonstrations 2 and 3 change rank 1 to 6.
The largest objects, of sizes 9, 5, and 6 respectively, become 9; every smaller object becomes 8.
Width-1 objects become 9, the width-2 L in demonstration 2 becomes 5, and width-3 rectangles and rings become 6.
All hole-free objects become 7; the one-hole ring in demonstration 2 becomes 5.
Widths 1, 2, and 3 become 7, 9, and 8 respectively, including the vertical line, square, and cross in demonstration 3.
Smallest objects become 9, including both tied size-3 objects in demonstration 2; largest and other objects become 8.
Every demonstrated object has zero holes and becomes 5, across single pixels, lines, squares, L shapes, and crosses.
The largest object becomes 6 in each demonstration; all smallest and intermediate objects become 8.
Pixel counts 2, 3, and 6 become 7, 8, and 9 respectively; size-4 squares and the size-9 square retain their colours.
